questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Slovakia?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Slovakia article.

questions.proof: Its capital city is Bratislava, the only capital of the world that borders two other countries.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Slovakia?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Slovakia on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Slovakia article.

questions.proof: It is bordered by Austria in the southwest, Hungary in the south, Ukraine in the east, Poland in the north and Czech Republic in the northwest.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Slovakia?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Slovakia article.

questions.proof: Slovakia (Official name The Slovak Republic, Slovenská republika) is a landlocked country in the eastern region of Central Europe.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Slovakia has been a member of the European Union since _____ and its official currency is the Euro.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twenty-first century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Slovakia article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: Slovakia has been a member of the European Union since May 1, 2004.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The Hungarian kings started to invite other settlers, for example Germans in the 13th century, and many others started to arrive in the kingdom, Vlachs from _____ in the 14th century and Jews.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Vlachs”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Slovakia article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: The Hungarian kings started to invite other settlers, for example Germans in the 13th century, and many others started to arrive in the kingdom, Vlachs from Romania in the 14th century and Jews.
